event.summary: Removing the host-premise watch does not permit a silent xterm fallback
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: Considered whether deleting the per-socket grid-premise watch and openTerminal's grid assertion would let browser tests pass using the retired terminal renderer. Source checks: the assigned patches remove HostPremiseWatch, its evidence fixture, and the shared-session assertion; the same revision's crates/farhelm-ui/assets/terminal.js mounts a grid component (around 3273-3393), its island element/focus helpers use island.grid (736-743), and its source has no xterm renderer path. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal widget: the grid island, opens with the exact contract: 'Every terminal runs in a terminal host ("Terminal host") and is interpreted by the supervisor’s emulator, so the browser draws a grid stream with its own grid client' (the source uses an ASCII apostrophe in supervisor's). Terminal host says: 'every terminal the supervisor serves is a host. Old tmux terminals, which earlier supervisors created, are ended when this release starts'. The deleted watch existed to distinguish the two renderers; after the renderer deletion this particular silent fallback cannot occur. Suggested bucket: other if it were a test-premise gap; could-be-highest: no, the concern is confined to maintainer tooling and no catastrophic route was identified. Confidence: confirmed by source, not execution. proposed_drop: replacement has no xterm renderer to fall back to; the quoted contract agrees with that source. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not searched. Caveat: this does not establish that all malformed grid streams are detected, only refutes the lost dual-renderer assertion concern.

event.summary: Host-menu timeout does not bound the panel-opening prelude, but the new caller already establishes that premise
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: Considered whether the new one-second menu timeout still lets a vanished panel consume the provisioning test's retry budget. openMenuPanel passes the timeout into getAttribute, hover, click, visibility, evaluate, and the measured-state poll (1353-1399). openHostMenu first calls showHostsPanel without that timeout (1444), whose toggle visibility wait is 20 seconds (1211-1215), but the only new bounded caller, provisioning.spec.ts:3781, has already opened Hosts at 3756 and established both busy rows at 3787-3788; only the menu flyout disappears as connection evidence reshapes rows. SPEC_impl.md's GUI contract says a row menu 'closes on any layout change that could have moved the row it was measured against'; closing the menu does not unmount the host panel. The intended vanished-flyout path is bounded by the new options; absence of the whole host panel is not the documented caller premise. Suggested bucket: other; could-be-highest: no, this is a test wait with no destructive effect. Confidence: confirmed by source, not execution. proposed_drop: no affected route in the new caller; the timeout is documented as per-operation, not an overall function deadline. possible_cover: none. Caveat: a future caller needing a deadline for initially opening Hosts would also need to bound showHostsPanel.
